subject: PDC Quiz 2 (12 March)
description: Quiz on OLAP, dashboards, data variety, concurrency, distributed systems, and MapReduce.

questions.text: A manager analyzes yearly sales trends. Which system fits?
questions.explanation: OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) is designed for complex queries on large datasets to support decision-making. Analyzing yearly sales trends is a classic analytical workload — aggregating historical data across dimensions like time, product, and region.
questions.shortExplanation: OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) is designed for complex queries on large datasets to support decision-making.

questions.explanation: Dashboards display aggregated metrics, trends, and KPIs — all of which require analytical queries over large datasets. OLAP systems are optimized for these read-heavy, multi-dimensional queries, making them the backbone of analytical dashboards.
questions.shortExplanation: Dashboards display aggregated metrics, trends, and KPIs — all of which require analytical queries over large datasets. OLAP systems are optimized for these read-heavy, multi-dimensional queries, making them the backbone of analytical dashboards.

questions.text: Combining structured and unstructured data reflects?
questions.explanation: Variety refers to the different forms of data — structured (tables), semi-structured (JSON/XML), and unstructured (images, text, logs). When you combine these different types, you're dealing with the Variety dimension of Big Data.
questions.shortExplanation: Variety refers to the different forms of data — structured (tables), semi-structured (JSON/XML), and unstructured (images, text, logs). When you combine these different types, you're dealing with the Variety dimension of Big Data.

questions.explanation: Context switching is the process of saving and restoring the state of a thread or process so another can run. This overhead (saving registers, flushing caches, etc.) directly reduces concurrency performance, since CPU time is spent switching rather than doing useful work.
questions.shortExplanation: Context switching is the process of saving and restoring the state of a thread or process so another can run.

questions.explanation: Distributed computing spreads tasks across multiple networked machines, allowing them to work simultaneously on different parts of a problem. This inherently increases parallelism — more nodes means more tasks can execute concurrently.
questions.shortExplanation: Distributed computing spreads tasks across multiple networked machines, allowing them to work simultaneously on different parts of a problem. This inherently increases parallelism — more nodes means more tasks can execute concurrently.

questions.explanation: A distributed system is composed of independent nodes (computers) connected via a network. Each node has its own processor, memory, and storage, and they coordinate through message passing to achieve a common goal.
questions.shortExplanation: A distributed system is composed of independent nodes (computers) connected via a network. Each node has its own processor, memory, and storage, and they coordinate through message passing to achieve a common goal.

questions.explanation: IoT devices (sensors, wearables, smart appliances) generate continuous streams of data at high speed. This rapid rate of data generation and the need for real-time processing is the defining characteristic of the Velocity dimension.
questions.shortExplanation: IoT devices (sensors, wearables, smart appliances) generate continuous streams of data at high speed. This rapid rate of data generation and the need for real-time processing is the defining characteristic of the Velocity dimension.

questions.text: Images, videos, and logs together illustrate?
questions.explanation: Images (binary), videos (multimedia), and logs (semi-structured text) are all different data formats. Having multiple data types and formats in a dataset is the hallmark of the Variety dimension of Big Data.
questions.shortExplanation: Images (binary), videos (multimedia), and logs (semi-structured text) are all different data formats. Having multiple data types and formats in a dataset is the hallmark of the Variety dimension of Big Data.

questions.explanation: MapReduce divides a large task into smaller sub-tasks (Map phase) that run in parallel across a cluster of machines, then combines results (Reduce phase). Adding more nodes to the cluster directly enhances parallelism and processing throughput.
questions.shortExplanation: MapReduce divides a large task into smaller sub-tasks (Map phase) that run in parallel across a cluster of machines, then combines results (Reduce phase). Adding more nodes to the cluster directly enhances parallelism and processing throughput.

questions.explanation: The core idea of MapReduce is parallel processing. The Map function processes input data splits in parallel across many nodes, and the Reduce function aggregates the intermediate results — enabling efficient processing of massive datasets.
questions.shortExplanation: The core idea of MapReduce is parallel processing. The Map function processes input data splits in parallel across many nodes, and the Reduce function aggregates the intermediate results — enabling efficient processing of massive datasets.
